title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1969-06-21
lineage: Early Show: AUD > MR > C > R > R > R > D > CD > EAC > SHN; Late Show: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Muddy audience recording of the first set contrasts with a crisp soundboard second half; classic early‑Dead acoustic/ country vibe shines with standout China Cat Sunflower, Old Old House and a smoking King Bee.
ai_review.review: The show captures an intriguing transitional period for the Dead – a mellow, pedal‑steel‑laden first set that suffers from a very muddy audience tape, followed by a crystal‑clear soundboard second set that delivers classic performances of China Cat Sunflower, Old Old House and a smoking King Bee. Reviewers rave about Jerry’s pedal‑steel work and the rare acoustic moments, while noting that the poor first‑set audio makes the overall listening experience mixed.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong musical highlights and historic value boost the rating, but inconsistent recording quality (muddy audience tape vs. crisp soundboard) drags it down; overall sentiment is mixed.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First set is an audience tape – very muddy and almost unlistenable. Second set is a clean, crisp soundboard recording but the overall release is incomplete and uneven.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Begins with a country‑rock acoustic feel (pedal steel, Green Green Grass) that transitions into psychedelic jams via China Cat Sunflower. The second set maintains the high energy and features rare acoustic/partial sets, making it the highlight despite the first half’s audio issues.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for pedal‑steel work and soaring guitar on China Cat Sunflower; described as “ripping” and taking the jam to another level.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted singing lead on Dire Wolf and involvement in acoustic moments.
